subject: Zenith commit fit: tokens/sec model & GPU headroom
messages:
From: Elena Soto <elena@zenith.ai>
To: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@zenith.ai
Date: Wed, 10 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Sizing request — expected TPS and p95 fit for committed capacity

Hi Priyom,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We are working through committed capacity sizing for our LLM-driven insights product and need a concrete throughput/latency model to evaluate the Dedicated offer. High-level context:
- Model: fine-tuned 33B transformer (similar to Llama2-33b backbone)
- Typical prompt length: 120 tokens + KV cache hit (many repeated contexts)
- Average completion length: 80 tokens
- Expected steady-state traffic: 1,200 concurrent users with an average of 0.4 requests/min/user (bursty peaks expected)
- Required SLO: p95 latency <= 450ms for completions above 256 tokens

Can you provide tokens/sec estimates, p95 latency mapping, and an initial headroom/gpu-slab recommendation for a committed monthly package? We want to align the commit size to minimize overprovisioning while staying within the SLA.

Also loop in any sizing artifacts you have.

Best,
Elena Soto
Head of Infrastructure
Zenith Analytics
From: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Soto <elena@zenith.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 10 Mar 2027 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Sizing request — expected TPS and p95 fit for committed capacity

Elena —

Thanks, this is great context. Quick reply with a high-level sketch before we run the workbook for exact numbers.

Key assumptions I'll use:
- Model latency characteristics (baseline): 0.8ms/token on H100 int8 optimized inference path at seq length ~200 using our runtime with continuous batching.
- Effective tokens/sec per H100 (single GPU, steady-state batch-friendly workload): ~1,200 tok/s.
- With KV-cache and prefix reuse we expect ~1.6x effective tokens/sec for many requests (your repeated contexts).
- P95 includes queueing under concurrency and batching; estimate p95 token latency for 256-token completion target at ~380–420ms on well-provisioned slab.

Immediate ask: can Marissa and I run a quick token workload model with your expected concurrency distribution? If you have a typical hourly traffic CSV that helps.

I'll attach a first-pass workbook for review.

Cheers,
Priyom
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Soto <elena@zenith.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 11 Mar 2027 09:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Sizing request — expected TPS and p95 fit for committed capacity

Elena —

I ran a short scenario set in the attached workbook (zenith_throughput_model.xlsx). Summary below — I kept each step explicit so you can inspect the inputs:

Inputs used (sheet: assumptions):
- Baseline per-token latency: 0.8ms on H100 int8 (inference path with our batching kernel)
- Baseline tok/s per H100: 1,200 tok/s (single stream steady-state)
- KV cache multiplier: 1.6x when cache reuse > 40%
- Average completion tokens: 80; p95 completion target considered at 256 tokens for worst-case
- Concurrent active requests at steady-state: 480 (1,200 users * 0.4 req/min = 480 r/min -> converted to concurrency with average latency)

Scenarios (all include 20% headroom for safety unless noted):
1) Baseline commit: target tokens/sec = 1,200 users * 0.4 req/min * 200 tokens/request = 1,600 tok/s.
   - Effective tok/s with KV cache: 2,560 tok/s.
   - Recommended committed GPUs: 3 H100s (3 * 1,200 * 1.6 = 5,760 effective tok/s) — *this overshoots; see note*.

2) Conservative commit (target minimizing SLO risk): plan for p95 headroom to handle 2x peak bursts -> provision 6 H100s => 6 * 1,200 * 1.6 = 11,520 effective tok/s. Estimated p95 for 256-token completion: ~320–380ms.

3) Cost-minimal commit (rely on burst/burst-bucket): commit 2 H100s + burstable credits (recommended for first 3 months). Estimated p95 at commit capacity: ~520–640ms (likely misses SLO during sustained peaks).

Notes:
- The single-GPU tok/s number is conservative for the model family; if you accept quantization to 4-bit and smaller batch windows we can push per-GPU throughput up ~25–30% (adjust workbook).
- Network egress and multi-region fallbacks are not in this simple model; if you need multiregion capacity add a 10% buffer.
- Our dedicated slabs enable automatic overflow to host pool (pay-as-you-go) if you want aggressive commits with safety net.

Attached: zenith_throughput_model.xlsx (scenario sheets), slo-fit-diagram.png (visual mapping), mutual_action_plan.pdf (next steps + timelines).

Happy to hop on a 30m call to walk through the workbook.

—Marissa
Sr Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Soto <elena@zenith.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 15 Mar 2027 08:33:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Sizing request — expected TPS and p95 fit for committed capacity

Elena —

Appreciate the dataset — quick commercial note so the sizing ties to the deal: if Zenith is comfortable with the Conservative commit (6 H100 slabs) we can offer a 12-month reserved plan at a 22% discount vs list Dedicated hourly. That includes:
- SLA: 99.9% uptime for the committed slab
- 15% burst credits per month for temporary peaks
- Quarterly review and tuning session with Marissa's team

If you want to start with the Baseline commit and add a burst buffer, we can structure a 6mo pilot with a path to convert to the 12mo reserved contract.

Let us know which scenario you prefer and we'll route legal/procurement.

Cheers,
Ben Carter
Senior Sales
From: Elena Soto <elena@zenith.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, procurement@zenith.ai
Date: Tue, 16 Mar 2027 10:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Sizing request — expected TPS and p95 fit for committed capacity

Thanks team — the workbook helped. A few follow-ups from procurement and engineering:
1) Procurement: can you send the draft SOW and commitment language for the 12-month reserved plan? We want explicit burst credit accounting and SLAs.
2) Engineering: can Marissa confirm the estimate if we flip to 4-bit quantization (we are sensitive to cost)? Also show p95 tradeoffs if we remove the 20% safety buffer.

For next steps, we're inclined toward the Conservative commit to meet product SLAs but would like to validate the quantization tradeoff to see if a 4 or 5 GPU commit could be possible with 4-bit (and with a slightly higher burst credit allocation).

Elena
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Soto <elena@zenith.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 17 Mar 2027 15:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Sizing request — expected TPS and p95 fit for committed capacity

Elena — quick follow-up with the adjusted scenarios attached in the same workbook (sheet: quantization). TL;DR:
- 4-bit path increases per-GPU effective tok/s by ~28% (H100) in our profiling for this model — realistic numbers: 1,540 tok/s baseline -> 1,970 tok/s effective with KV cache.
- Conservative commit re-evaluated: 5 H100s at 4-bit yields ~5 * 1,970 = 9,850 effective tok/s -> estimated p95 for 256-token completion: ~350ms. That's within your 450ms SLO and reduces commit size vs 6 H100s.
- Removing the 20% safety buffer: expect p95 variance to widen to 380–430ms under network variability; still within SLO but less comfortable for sustained bursts.

Recommendation: sign the 12-month reserved 5-H100 plan with an explicit burst credit pool (we recommend 25% monthly burst allocation while you ramp). We'll prepare the SOW and the exact billing schedule; Ben, can you circulate the draft contract?

I attached an updated mutual_action_plan.pdf with milestones and a DocuSign link for signature.

—Marissa
(end of thread)
